result.title: Evaluating Bayesian deep learning for robust biomedical time-series classification under distribution shift: A sleep scoring case study
result.comment: 28 pages (8 pages main text), 8 figures, 15 tables
result.summary: In biomedical time-series classification, machine learning models often suffer from deteriorating accuracy and calibration due to distribution shift. We investigate to what degree Bayesian-inspired deep learning improves robustness through Bayesian model averaging (BMA). Using rodent sleep scoring as a case study, we evaluate BMA under distribution shifts in genotype, laboratory, and species. We systematically compare nine approximate inference methods spanning single- and multi-basin approaches across two neural network backbones on in-distribution (ID) data and five out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets. In our results, multi-basin methods perform best, outperforming baselines and single-basin methods. Compared with point estimates, BMA generally improves OOD accuracy and calibration across both architectures, while yielding only modest ID gains. It also often improves selective prediction and OOD and artifact detection, but, interestingly, not inter-rater disagreement detection.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以啮齿动物睡眠分期为案例，在两种骨干网络上比较九种近似推断方法（单盆地与多盆地），评估贝叶斯模型平均在基因型、实验室与物种分布偏移下的准确率、校准、选择性预测和 OOD／伪迹检测表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其不确定性校准与选择性预测评测，可能为 LVR 中「置信度是否足以停止推理、是否需继续获取视觉证据」的判据设计提供参照，但论文属生物医学时序领域，迁移价值需核查。
